scale.title: Scale
scale.subtitle: Increase or reduce the number of copies (replicas) of an application.
scale.how1: More replicas mean more capacity and more resilience to failures; fewer replicas free resources. Kubernetes starts or stops Pods to reach the requested number.
scale.how2: Scaling to 0 stops the application: an explicit confirmation is required.
scale.hpaHint: This application is managed by a HorizontalPodAutoscaler: manually set replicas will be corrected automatically within the min–max limits.
scale.hpaNote: If an application has a HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA), the HPA decides the number of replicas based on load: to change it permanently edit the HPA.

restart.title: Restart
restart.subtitle: Restart an application progressively (rolling restart).
restart.how1: Kubernetes replaces the Pods one at a time following the update strategy: a new Pod starts and, once ready, an old one is terminated.
restart.how2: With at least 2 replicas and readiness probes there is no outage. With a single replica there may be a short interruption. Useful for example to reload a changed ConfigMap or Secret.

rollout.title: Rollout
rollout.subtitle: Update status, revision history and rollback of Deployments.
rollout.pick: Pick a Deployment to see its rollout status and history.
rollout.complete: Rollout complete: all replicas use revision {{revision}}.
rollout.pausedText: The rollout is paused: template changes are not applied until you resume it.
rollout.inProgress: Update in progress: {{ready}} of {{desired}} replicas ready. The page refreshes automatically.
rollout.recreate: Recreate (old Pods are stopped before new ones start)
rollout.resumeFirst: Resume the rollout before rolling back
rollout.compareHint: Left: template of the current revision {{a}}; right: revision {{b}}.
rollout.explain1: Every change to a Deployment template (image, variables, resources) creates a new revision, applied by progressively replacing the Pods.
rollout.explain2: Rollback re-applies the template of a previous revision with a new progressive update: it does not restore data or volumes.

yaml.title: Apply YAML
yaml.subtitle: Advanced mode: apply Kubernetes manifests with validation, diff and confirmation.
yaml.validServer: Valid configuration: Kubernetes accepted it in dry-run mode (no change applied).
yaml.validLocal: Valid structure. Cluster validation was not run because your role cannot apply these resources.
yaml.conflictText: Some fields are managed by another tool (e.g. kubectl, Helm, an operator). Forcing the apply overwrites them: the original tool may revert them or behave unexpectedly.
yaml.forceAdminOnly: Only an Administrator can force the apply.
yaml.forceCons1: Conflicting fields move under Scarlet management.
yaml.forceCons2: The tool that managed them may overwrite them again.
yaml.diffNote: Left: current state in the cluster (without status fields); right: the document to apply. Fields not in the document are left unchanged (server-side apply).
yaml.cons1: Resources are created or updated in the cluster with server-side apply.
yaml.cons2: Workload changes start a progressive update of the Pods.
yaml.cons3: The operation is recorded in the audit log.
yaml.templateHint: Inserts a commented example for the chosen resource type.
yaml.templateSteps: Edit the values (name, data, image…) following the comments, then press Validate for the cluster check, Differences to see what changes and Apply to create it.

backup.title: Backup
backup.subtitle: Backup of the Scarlet application: status, history, verification and restore procedure.
backup.what1: The Scarlet database: users, roles, audit log, settings, notifications and backup history.
backup.what2: Configuration files (config.yaml and pkm.env, which may contain secrets: the archive is readable only by the service).
backup.what3: Optional: an export of the Kubernetes manifests of the applications (Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, …) as YAML.
backup.not1: It is not a full Kubernetes backup: etcd and the cluster state are not included.
backup.not2: Persistent volume (PV) data is not included.
backup.not3: Kubernetes Secrets are not exported. For a cluster backup use etcd snapshots or Velero.
backup.includeHint: The backup runs in the background; backups older than the retention are deleted automatically.
backup.manageOnly: Only an Administrator can run, verify, download or delete backups.
backup.verifyOkText: The archive is intact: checksums match and the database is readable.
backup.verifyFailText: The archive is NOT intact: do not use it for a restore.
backup.deleteCons: The archive and its checksum are permanently deleted from disk.
backup.restoreExplain: Restore replaces the Scarlet database and is run from the server shell with the service stopped, to avoid concurrent writes. The script verifies the archive before proceeding and keeps a copy of the current database.
backup.restoreSelected: Click a row of the history to put that file in the command.
backup.scheduledText: The daily automatic backup is run by the systemd timer pkm-backup.timer. To check it:

maint.title: Maintenance
maint.subtitle: Put nodes in maintenance safely and maintain the application.
maint.how1: Cordon: the node receives no new Pods.
maint.how2: Drain: Pods are moved to other nodes respecting PodDisruptionBudgets.
maint.how3: After the maintenance: Uncordon to put the node back in service.
maint.nodesAdminOnly: Only an Administrator can cordon, uncordon and drain.
maint.drainExplain: Drain puts the node in maintenance and moves its Pods to other nodes through the Eviction API: PodDisruptionBudgets are respected (if an eviction would violate them, Scarlet retries while possible or until the timeout). DaemonSet Pods stay on the node.

reasons.daemonset: DaemonSet Pod: it must run on every node, it stays.
reasons.mirror_pod: Static Pod managed directly by the kubelet.
reasons.unmanaged: Pod without controller: if evicted it will NOT be recreated.
reasons.emptydir: Uses an emptyDir volume: its temporary data will be lost.

maint.forceUnmanaged: Also evict Pods without controller (they will not be recreated)
maint.deleteEmptydir: Also evict Pods with emptyDir (temporary data will be lost)
maint.blocked: {{count}} Pods prevent the drain: enable the matching option or handle them manually.
maint.drainRisk: Applications with a single replica on the node will have a short outage. Check that the other nodes have enough capacity.

step.retry: Pod {{pod}} protected by a PodDisruptionBudget: retrying shortly

maint.timedOut: Timeout reached: some Pods were not moved (often because of a PodDisruptionBudget).
maint.afterDrain: The node stays in maintenance: when the work is done use Uncordon.
maint.appExplain: Safe operations on the Scarlet database and cache. They do not touch the cluster.

housekeeping.title: Clean up expired data
housekeeping.text: Deletes expired sessions, audit entries beyond retention and notifications resolved more than 30 days ago.
housekeeping.cons: Deleted data cannot be recovered (except from a backup).

cache.title: Clear cache
cache.text: Forces data to be re-read from Kubernetes on the next request.
cache.cons: Next pages may load slightly slower.

db.title: Optimize database
db.text: Checks the database integrity (PRAGMA integrity_check) and compacts it (VACUUM).
db.cons: Writes are briefly suspended during the operation.
